external_entities.name: insurance partner
external_entities.description: One of three insurance partners that provides a daily extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Three insurance partners drop a daily extract for us.
external_entities.notes: The text refers to three partners but does not identify them individually.

external_entities.name: analyst
external_entities.description: An analyst who queries the warehouse directly.
external_entities.notes: Analysts authenticate with SSO and are on the warehouse network.

processes.name: Airflow scheduler
processes.description: A scheduler that lists and reads files from the landing bucket and triggers a Spark transform job.
processes.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there.
processes.notes: The scheduler does not check that a file came from the partner whose folder it landed in. Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

processes.name: Spark transform job
processes.description: A Spark job that normalizes claim records and loads them into BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.
processes.notes: Nothing validates the row contents beyond the schema.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket receiving daily partner extracts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_stores.notes: The submitter said: "I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted ... Both are on defaults as far as I know."

data_stores.name: Airflow metadata database
data_stores.description: Airflow's metadata database containing connection strings and partner keys.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
data_stores.notes: The submitter said: "I don't know ... whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest. Both are on defaults as far as I know."

data_stores.name: BigQuery
data_stores.description: The warehouse containing normalized claim records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.
data_stores.notes: Analysts have a dataset-wide grant and member-identifying columns have not been split out.

assumptions.assumption: The insurance partner is represented as an external system because it pushes files into the landing bucket.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the partner as an actor that pushes files over SFTP, but the schema permits only human or external-system.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contains confidential data because its extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow metadata database contains confidential data because it stores connection strings and partner keys.
assumptions.basis: The source states that Airflow keeps connection strings and partner keys in the metadata database.

assumptions.assumption: BigQuery contains confidential data because it stores claim records with member names and dates of birth.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the transform loads normalized claim records into BigQuery, and the extracts contain member names and dates of birth.

assumptions.assumption: SFTP provides encryption in transit intrinsically.
assumptions.basis: The source names SFTP as the protocol; the extraction rules specify that SFTP's intrinsic encryption is recorded.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow scheduler presents a non-web interface because it is described as a scheduler and batch-style process.
assumptions.basis: The source describes Airflow as a scheduler that wakes, lists, reads, and triggers processing rather than as a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The Spark transform job presents a non-web interface because it is described as a transform job.
assumptions.basis: The source describes Spark as a transform job that normalizes records and loads them into BigQuery.
